stories.h: Primetime: Pattinson's Chris Hansen is a career best
stories.why: Prestige A24 drama with a big star turn
sum: Lance Oppenheim's Primetime restages the year To Catch A Predator was NBC's flagship show, with Robert Pattinson as host Chris Hansen, Merritt Wever as a ratings-obsessed producer and Skyler Gisondo as a struggling actor hired as a decoy. Little White Lies calls Pattinson's uncanny turn the best work of his career.

The review argues the film neither condemns nor excuses Hansen. Instead it looks at the show's appeal: ratings, celebrity and the public appetite for spectacle. It ties all this to post-9/11 disillusionment and to today's online vigilante culture, and finds the film's unsettling, self-aware style its strongest asset. It opens in UK cinemas on 30 October and runs 109 minutes.
pts: Scored 4/5 across the board by Little White Lies
Pattinson, Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo; 109 min
More about the hunger for spectacle than about justice

stories.h: I Love Boosters: Boots Riley's candy-coloured heist satire
sum: Boots Riley's new comedy follows the Velvet Gang, a trio of professional shoplifters who lift designer clothes and sell them on cheaply. Their leader, Corvette (KeKe Palmer), dreams of becoming a designer herself and sets her sights on fashion mogul Christie Smith (Demi Moore). Naomi Ackie, LaKeith Stanfield and Don Cheadle co-star.

Little White Lies praises the bold visuals and costume design, and the sharp swipes at how the fashion industry exploits people. It likes that the morality stays blurry: the rebels still crave what the system sells them. Its main complaint is that the film crams in too many jokes, arguments and messages, and Riley doesn't always know when to stop.
pts: KeKe Palmer, Naomi Ackie, Demi Moore; 114 min

stories.h: Possible Love: Lee Chang-dong's thorny class drama
sum: Lee Chang-dong's first feature in years follows two couples on opposite sides of Korea's class divide. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) and her husband are reeling from a mass layoff and a broken strike. Ye-ji, a documentary filmmaker married to a wealthy man, starts a film about the laid-off workers and befriends Mi-ok, and the gap between them grows harder to ignore.

Little White Lies finds it rich and layered. It says Lee captures domestic strain under corporate greed and automation with a bittersweet tone, quite unlike Park Chan-wook's satirical No Other Choice. The review singles out the film's question of who gets to tell other people's stories. It takes a while to find its rhythm over 166 minutes, but the ensemble is excellent.
pts: Jeon Do-yeon also has a Gotham Award lead-performance nomination
166 min; out now in UK cinemas

stories.h: Fatherland: Pawlikowski and Sandra Hüller go to postwar Germany
stories.why: Art-house auteur plus a standout actor
sum: Paweł Pawlikowski (Ida, Cold War) returns with another stark black-and-white, Academy-ratio drama. In 1949, novelist Thomas Mann comes back from exile in California to accept honours on both sides of a divided Germany. His daughter Erika, played by Sandra Hüller, travels with him and manages family crises over the phone.

Little White Lies sees it as a trim 82-minute portrait of a nation where former collaborators play down their past and regimes co-opt artists for prestige. It calls this a kind of culturewashing and links the film to Mephisto and The Zone of Interest. The review praises Hanns Zischler as Mann and argues Hüller may be the best actor working today.
pts: 4/5 across the board from Little White Lies
Hüller, Hanns Zischler, August Diehl; 82 min
Also up for a Gotham international feature award

stories.h: Letterboxd's 20 best films of the fall festivals
stories.why: Watchlist builder for the coming months
sum: Thirteen Letterboxd writers pick the 20 standouts from Venice, Telluride, TIFF, NYFF, London and other autumn festivals. The list includes Kore-eda's manga adaptation Look Back, Lee Chang-dong's Possible Love, Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine, Andrew Haigh's A Long Winter, and Mike Leigh's Tender Loving Care, which may be his last film. Also on it are Takashi Yamazaki's Godzilla Minus Zero and Luca Guadagnino's OpenAI drama Artificial.

The slate is strongly international, with Korean, Japanese, Tamil, Lebanese and Hungarian picks, and it is rich in documentaries. Those include NAZA on AI-driven targeting in Gaza and the Elizabeth Holmes film You Can See Everything. Some titles, such as Herzog's Bucking Fastard, still lack US distribution.
pts: 20 picks, including Look Back, Godzilla Minus Zero and Possible Love
Tamil drama Dorothy is rated 4.1 on Letterboxd
A ready-made watchlist for awards season

stories.h: Jeff Nichols looks back on Take Shelter at 15
stories.why: Director deep-dive on a modern cult favourite
sum: For Take Shelter's 15th anniversary, which comes with a new Blu-ray and digital release, Jeff Nichols tells Letterboxd how the film grew from the 2008 financial crisis and his own anxious start to adulthood. He shot it for under $1 million in 24 days. Nichols describes it as a film about everyone's mental health, not just mental illness, and about a husband's silence inside a marriage.

He recalls Jessica Chastain's emotional presence, studio notes he found baffling, and early Sundance audiences laughing at the tense Lions Club scene. He still sees the ending as hopeful. He also explains why he won't test-screen his films, and says his next one, King Snake, has a no-test-screening clause in its contract.
pts: Made for under $1m in 24 shooting days
Nichols reads the ending as hopeful
No test screenings for his next film, King Snake

stories.h: Jafar Panahi handed new five-year prison sentence
sum: According to his lawyer, a Tehran Revolutionary Court has sentenced Palme d'Or winner Jafar Panahi in absentia to five years and one month in prison. The ruling also seizes his assets and imposes a two-year travel ban and a two-year social media ban. His team found out only after his bank accounts were frozen, and the charges have not been made public.

The court described Panahi as abroad and unreachable, although he has been back in Iran since March. He now faces three separate legal cases, including a December 2025 propaganda conviction that was upheld on appeal. His latest film, It Was Just An Accident, won the 2025 Palme d'Or and two Oscar nominations.
pts: 5 years 1 month, plus travel and social media bans
Sentenced without being told of the hearing
Panahi is in Iran and faces three ongoing cases

stories.h: Oscars to add more festivals as international-feature routes
stories.why: Opens more Oscar routes for Asian films
sum: At the Tokyo International Film Festival, Academy CEO Bill Kramer said the Academy plans to add more festivals whose top prizes can qualify a film for the international feature Oscar. Asked whether Tokyo might join the list, he said only to stay tuned. Since a May rule change, non-English-language winners at Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto and Venice can be submitted alongside each country's official pick.

Academy leaders added that non-US members now make up 25% of the roughly 11,000 voters, up from 5% a decade ago. They also said the Oscars move to YouTube in 2029, and that a theatrical release will still be required for eligibility.
pts: Six festivals already qualify, Busan among them

stories.h: Sundance 2027 to revive Memento and Y Tu Mamá También
sum: Sundance's first Colorado edition runs 21–31 January 2027, and its Legacy Program will mark anniversaries of films from the festival's archive. New 4K restorations of Y Tu Mamá También, Better Luck Tomorrow, Dogtown and Z-Boys and Real Women Have Curves get 25th-anniversary screenings. Fool's Fire, Nitrate Kisses and Swoon mark 35 years.

Christopher Nolan's Memento will screen as an interactive Cinema Interruptus session, where audience members can call for pauses to discuss the film. Letterboxd is co-presenting the strand, which runs 27–31 January.

stories.h: Gotham Award nominations: The Invite and Tender Loving Care lead
sum: The Invite, All Of A Sudden, Clarissa, La Gradiva and Mike Leigh's Tender Loving Care lead the 36th Gotham Award nominations with four nods each. The best feature shortlist includes Primetime, The Debut and Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. Possible Love, Fatherland and Ryusuke Hamaguchi's All Of A Sudden are in the international race.

The best director nominees are Hamaguchi, Leigh, Andrey Zvyagintsev, Sandra Wollner and Jane Schoenbrun. Lead-performance nominees include Jeon Do-yeon, Julianne Moore and John Turturro. The audience award returns, with Project Hail Mary and La Bola Negra among the contenders. Winners will be named in New York on 30 November.
pts: Five films lead with four nominations each
Asian contenders include Hamaguchi and Jeon Do-yeon

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: PISS's debut earns a perfect score
sum: The Line of Best Fit gives a rare 10/10 to you made me / skin on linen, the debut from noise-rock duo PISS: vocalist Taylor Zantingh and guitarist Tyler Paterson. Most of its 15 tracks run two minutes or less, building and collapsing noise-punk textures with slowcore patience. Zantingh's voice swings between screams, gasps and manic yelling.

Between songs, recordings of feminist thinkers and organisers sit over ambient collages. The album confronts sexual violence, abuse and misogyny head-on, and the climax, "blocking a scene you can't remember", builds from a Slint-like arrangement into raw recollection. The reviewer calls it uncompromising but not hopeless. It's out 30 October.
pts: For fans of Slint, METZ and confrontational noise-rock
Start with "blocking a scene you can't remember"
stories.q: PISS you made me / skin on linen

stories.h: DIIV go lighter on ZIRP!, with mixed results
sum: DIIV's new album ZIRP!, produced by A. G. Cook, swaps their blown-out shoegaze for a leaner, pop-tinged sound the band calls "The New Alternative". The Line of Best Fit gives it 6/10. The lyrics turn outward to economic collapse and inequality, picking up themes from 2024's Frog in Boiling Water, but the reviewer finds them blunter than before.

"Kid" is the highlight, blending Cook's polish with DIIV's dream-pop, and "When the Glow Came for Us" also lands. "Trillions" will divide listeners. The critic calls the record an overcorrection: the stripped-back approach leaves room to experiment but loses much of what made DIIV special. Stereogum disagreed and made it Album of the Week. It's out 30 October on Fantasy.
pts: Critics split: Stereogum's Album of the Week, 6/10 here
For fans of Deceiver-era DIIV and nu-gaze

stories.h: Queens of the Stone Age close the album cycle with a Dave Grohl track
sum: Queens of the Stone Age have shared "Run Away From The Mob", the last single before their new album Perfecth arrives 30 October on Matador. It closes the record, but it dates back to the 2013 ...Like Clockwork sessions and has Dave Grohl on drums.

Josh Homme describes it as a letter to his eldest son with final instructions in case everything goes wrong. It's about mob mentality and the court of public opinion, and it moves from a mournful guitar figure to a fierce declaration of loyalty. It follows the earlier single "Where The Goth Girls At?".
stories.q: Queens of the Stone Age Run Away From The Mob

stories.h: Sam Burton's Fairweather Friend makes old-school folk feel fresh
stories.why: Quiet indie-folk pick for the commute
sum: Sam Burton's third album gets an 8/10 from The Line of Best Fit. It's warm, unfussy folk with touches of country and classic rock: his melancholy voice and rippling acoustic guitar out front, pedal steel drifting in, and Jonathan Wilson co-producing some tracks.

The songs grew out of a car crash, then a spell of travel and farm work in northern California, and they dwell on impermanence and restless freedom. The reviewer points to early-'70s Dylan, Gordon Lightfoot and Neil Young's Comes A Time, and argues the songwriting is strong enough that it never feels like mere retro copying. It's out 30 October.
pts: Start with "Start Over", the album's peak
"Lilac Man" is a striking solo acoustic piece
For fans of Neil Young and Jonathan Wilson

stories.h: Kilby Block Party 2027: Deftones, The Strokes, Jungle
sum: Utah's indie-leaning Kilby Block Party has announced its 2027 lineup for 14–16 May at the Utah State Fairpark. Deftones, The Strokes and Jungle headline, with Fontaines D.C., Slayyyter and Lil Yachty just below. Two Door Cinema Club will play Tourist History in full and Whitney will play Light Upon The Lake.

The deep bill includes Spoon, Kim Gordon, Hot Chip, Wolf Parade, IDLES, Weyes Blood, Julien Baker, Wednesday, Iceage, Atlas Sound and The Radio Dept. Several question marks on the poster hint at reunions still to be revealed. General on-sale opens 29 October at 10am Mountain Time.
pts: Full-album sets from Two Door Cinema Club and Whitney

stories.h: The Chats announce new album Half Cut
sum: Australian punks The Chats will release Half Cut, the follow-up to 2022's Get Fucked, on 5 March 2027 via Virgin Music Group. They recorded it in Los Angeles with Jay Whalley of Frenzal Rhomb, and frontman Eamon Sandwith calls it a fun rock and roll record that's a bit more open than their past work.

The first single, "Off It", is quick and catchy and comes with a video by Matt Weston. The album has 14 tracks. The band just toured with Social Distortion and Descendents and plays an Australian run from 13 November to 13 December.
pts: For fans of Amyl and the Sniffers

stories.h: GANGGA tells three stories of loss on a new maxi-single
sum: Indonesian singer-songwriter GANGGA has released 5 hours apart, 2017, a three-track maxi-single that leads into his second album. "Dear April" is about giving everything to a relationship and still being left. "I Will" mourns someone who has died and the time that was lost. The lead track, "Moonlight", imagines a dreamlike reunion.

LA producer Spathies worked on two tracks and Will Mara on the third. Documentary-style visuals of portraits, quiet rooms and broken objects come with the release. GANGGA links the story to his earlier songs "Blue Jeans" and "Whiskey Bottle". It's on streaming services now.

stories.h: Solo's The Innocent sings for the sandwich generation
sum: The Innocent, the solo project of Surakarta (Solo) musician Annang Fahmi, has released the single "Nanti Kau Kan Mengerti". It's about the sandwich generation, people torn between their own dreams and supporting family, and it draws on Annang's experience and his friends'. The message: putting goals on hold doesn't mean giving them up.

The piano-led track was co-written with Traffic Jam vocalist Bintang Aditya, with Rovega Krisna of Traffic Jam on piano. It was released 9 October and will appear on an EP due in 2027. Annang hopes to play the songs at Solo venues such as Sedayadi and Suaraga.
stories.q: The Innocent Nanti Kau Kan Mengerti

stories.h: Telfar drops a glow-in-the-dark Baby Bag Charm Friday
sum: Telfar's next small drop is a glow-in-the-dark version of its Baby Bag Charm, the mini shopper that clips onto a bigger bag or works as a tiny carry on its own. It goes live on Friday, October 30 at 11am New York time, which is Friday night (about 10pm) in Jakarta.

It joins a long run of charm colors already on the site, including Azalea, Acid, Ballerina, Black Rainbow, Yellow and a washed blue denim. Telfar is also pushing a Shmedium shopper restock, a new FW26 collection, $68 printed skullies (leopard, snake, star) and a free hat on orders over $200.

stories.h: PROTECT turns Salomon's ACS NEXT into a slushie
sum: London shop PROTECT has reworked Salomon's technical ACS NEXT trail runner around the candy colors of a frozen slushie drink. The upper fades from red into blue, with metallic silver overlays, white accents and pops of yellow, sitting on a blue midsole.
The trail-shoe build stays visible underneath, and PROTECT adds its own co-branding graphics. The colorway is named Lava Falls/Cyber Yellow, and it releases through PROTECT's own webstore.

stories.h: PUMA x NAHMIAS Suede Crochet adds three colorways
sum: PUMA and NAHMIAS are back with three new takes on their Suede Crochet: a tonal chocolate brown, a green suede with a bright yellow stripe, and an electric blue with yellow accents. Each has chunky multicolor crochet laces, a crocheted Formstrip, canvas details and a printed message in the lining, plus spare lace sets to swap.
The launch comes with playful pop-ups built around NAHMIAS's made-up Cornballs cereal, whose boxes hide collectibles, sneaker redemption tickets and $1,000 golden tickets.

stories.h: Salehe Bembury's SPUNGE Lumina lands in ocean-blue Cenote
sum: SPUNGE, Salehe Bembury's own footwear label, is launching its second original shoe, the Lumina, in a debut colorway called Cenote, an oceanic palette. It is about 15% lighter than the earlier Osmosis, with a single-layer mesh upper and caged squishy cushioning.

Signature SPUNGE details carry over, like the split line at the toe and textured touch zones. Bembury says he picked the color on instinct rather than data. Newsletter subscribers got early access on the 28th; everyone else can buy today.

stories.h: Corteiz x Nike Shox R419 gets a royal blue look
sum: Corteiz and Nike have shown the Game Royal version of the Shox R419, their reworked Shox R4. The upper has raised horizontal ridges, carbon-fiber panels and car-inspired details, and the Shox columns stay in the heel.
Branding includes a red C on the tongue and an R419 window at the heel, and every pair comes with a branded bolt washer. The blue/red/black pair sits alongside black and metallic silver versions.

stories.h: Wales Bonner x adidas FW26 drops today
sum: adidas Originals and Wales Bonner have a new Fall/Winter 2026 collection that revisits their past hits. Sneakers include a croc-stamped brown Karintha with gold hardware, a vivid green Gazelle Snake, a suede Adizero Adios and a pony-hair BW Pony with lizard print.

Clothing covers tracksuits, pinstripe track sets, football jerseys, stirrup track pants and a leather blouson, plus croc-embossed neoprene bags and lanyards. Harley Weir shot the campaign, inspired by 1980s London youth.

stories.h: Heeled trainers are climbing again
sum: Dazed looks at why trainers keep growing heels. The thread runs from Miu Miu's heeled football boots and Ancuta Sarca's stiletto hybrids to Converse x Vaquera's kitten-heel skate shoe and Martine Rose's lifted Nike Shox. Nike is also teasing the Ovolo 2.0, a 2004 shoe brought back with a taller heel, for 2027.

Wedge trainers are back too: Isabel Marant's Bekett wedge sneaker jumped 630% on Lyst last year. Onitsuka Tiger and Lacoste showed their own hybrids for SS27. The writer's verdict: fun as a trend piece, not a practical shoe.

stories.h: Ballhog: archive fashion that refuses to be serious
sum: Ballhog is a TikTok style that mixes rare archive pieces with 2010s swag and gaudy 2000s luxury, posted with silly edits, fart noises and electroclash. To most people the outfits look plain. The flex is knowing how rare the Number (N)ine, Undercover, Hysteric Glamour or Jeremy Scott pieces are.

The name comes from the Ball Hog Collective, friends who met on Discord over clothes and NBA 2K. Dazed sees it as a quieter heir to hypebeast culture, fed by resale, vintage and reps, and loved and mocked in equal measure.

stories.h: Cabinet Couture: the Instagram tracking Indonesia's elite
sum: Dazed profiles Cabinet Couture, an anonymous Instagram account that reposts photos of Indonesian officials wearing luxury goods, names each item and adds its price. It began in September 2025, days after protests sparked by the death of delivery rider Affan Kurniawan, and now has over 277,000 followers.

The original account was geo-blocked in Indonesia. The team compares officials' declared wealth with their visible spending, flags relatives handed parliamentary seats, and relies on tips from followers and luxury-industry insiders.

stories.h: Sophia Wilson shoots Dr. Martens' grunge girlhood
sum: Dr. Martens' With Bouncing Soles campaign celebrates the 1460 boot, first released in 1960. For it, photographer Sophia Wilson, a longtime fan, shot a portfolio called The Joy of Girlhood around the brand's Crazy Horse Leather collection.

Her portraits mix grunge with polished vintage styling. The 1460, the 1461 shoe and a holographic pair all appear. The project launched with a New York gallery party on October 8, with a DJ, Polaroids and custom keychains.

stories.h: #IndonesiaSadar: students rally nationwide on Youth Pledge Day
sum: Students and civil society groups protested in several cities on 28 October, the Sumpah Pemuda anniversary, two years into the Prabowo-Gibran government, Magdalene reports. In Jakarta, BEM UI and Komite Sadar led the action at the Hotel Indonesia roundabout under the slogan "Tepati atau Pergi" (keep your promises or go), with the three-finger salute as the signature gesture.

Their five demands: national disaster status for ecological crises and action against responsible corporations, budget money redirected from the free-meals and Merah Putih cooperative programs to public needs, cheaper education and decent jobs, an end to legal abuse and corruption, and restored free expression. Tribun Makassar counted at least 33 protest points in Makassar; actions were also planned in Yogyakarta and Bandung.
pts: Demands extend those of the 20 October protests
Amnesty's Usman Hamid called the slogan an expression of concern, not violence
Komnas HAM urged police to avoid excessive force

stories.h: Months of blackouts amid haze: Kalimantan residents sue PLN
sum: Since June, state utility PLN has run rolling blackouts across South and Central Kalimantan, overlapping with forest-fire haze, Project Multatuli reports. Early cuts lasted four to eight hours a day; PLN blamed failures at several power plants and repeatedly missed its own deadlines to end them. Farmers, bakers and families describe dead livestock, ruined crops and a smoke-sick infant moved around in search of power.

LBH Borneo Nusantara and Forkot Banjarmasin have sued PLN at the Banjarmasin administrative court, seeking compensation and accountability; PLN disputes the court's jurisdiction. Trend Asia links the crisis to coal export and smelter priorities under weak domestic-supply rules, while the mining experts' association blames technical faults.
pts: One poultry farmer says about 5,000 birds died
An academic projects Banjarmasin small-business losses near Rp15.5 billion a week
Outages were still continuing in October

stories.h: Two years of Prabowo: forests and Indigenous land under siege
sum: Mongabay Indonesia's two-year review argues forest governance has worsened under Prabowo, with this year's haze crisis as one symptom. Citing Auriga Nusantara, it says deforestation rose 66% in 2025 to about 433,751 hectares, and Walhi says 26.5 million hectares of forest sit under company control. Large food and energy estates, including about 2.7 million hectares in South Papua, are clearing customary land.

Experts quoted say permits and Strategic National Project labels legalise destruction, while Jatam documents 58 cases of military involvement in violence or land grabs against civilians in two years. BRWA data show only 7.5 million of 36.6 million hectares of claimed customary territory officially recognised.
pts: Military budget reportedly rose from Rp70 trillion to Rp200 trillion
1,147 people criminalised, intimidated or attacked in customary-land conflicts, 2015-2025
CIFOR expert says Indonesia is drifting from its zero-deforestation goal

stories.h: Fire crackdown punishes farmers, ignores haze victims
sum: Indonesia's enforcement against forest and land fires focuses on burned land and state revenue, not on people sickened or impoverished by smoke, experts told a Komnas HAM discussion reported by Mongabay Indonesia. UI law professor Andri Gunawan Wibisana said damages won from companies usually flow to state coffers rather than recovery, and that firms draining peat can face strict liability.

Environmental law group ICEL's review of 217 cases from 2019 to 2024 found prosecutions overwhelmingly hit individuals rather than corporations. Walhi counted hotspots across hundreds of concessions by September and urged Komnas HAM to push ministries to sue companies, citing two Dayak Maanyan farmers named as suspects.
pts: About 37.6 million ha of forest under permits vs 5-6 million ha for communities
Walhi wants companies named as suspects made public

stories.h: Record Palestinian vote leaves Netanyahu short of majority
sum: With nearly 90% of votes counted, no bloc has reached the 61 seats needed in Israel's Knesset, Al Jazeera reports. Netanyahu's bloc is on course for 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition for 48, while the Joint List and Ra'am are projected at a record 17 to 19 seats on high turnout among Palestinian citizens. Over 500,000 special ballots remain.

Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot ruled out governing with Arab-led parties. The Joint List says Arab turnout kept Netanyahu from a majority and it could back an anti-Netanyahu government from outside. Likud accused Arab parties of stealing the election and says it passed alleged evidence to police and the Shin Bet.
pts: Turnout in some Arab towns topped 70%, per Al Jazeera
Netanyahu stays caretaker PM; official results due next week
President Herzog urged parties to avoid another election

stories.h: Hebron lockdown hits day six as West Bank raids widen
sum: Israeli forces kept raiding Hebron neighbourhoods and surrounding towns as the lockdown of the West Bank's largest city entered its sixth day, Al Jazeera reports, citing Anadolu and Wafa. Troops detained four people in Tulkarem, including a journalist, fired tear gas at protesters opposing home demolitions in Beita, and turned homes in Burin into barracks. Schools in southern Nablus moved online.

UNRWA said the Hebron incursions have displaced nearly 5,000 Palestinians and warned that collective punishment violates international law. The operation followed the killing of two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint; Palestinian officials accuse Netanyahu of using it to court settler votes.
pts: Nearly 5,000 displaced in Hebron, per UNRWA
Over 34,000 refugees from northern camps still displaced since 2025, per UNRWA
Democracy Now also reports troops broke up a Hebron protest

stories.h: Issa Amro: Hebron's displacement as an election spectacle
sum: Hebron activist Issa Amro, founder of Youth Against Settlements, writes in +972 Magazine that Israel's operation since 23 October punishes civilians for an attack they had no part in. Citing the Hebron Municipality, he says about 3,971 people from 619 families were forced out, some given minutes to leave at night, his own sister's family among them.

Citing Wafa and the Palestinian Prisoners' Society, he reports 85 detentions, homes turned into military posts and about 100 shops shut. He argues Netanyahu and his far-right allies are staging toughness before the vote, and that the displacement will become permanent facts on the ground unless the world acts.
pts: About 86 acres destroyed or marked for demolition, per the municipality
Opinion piece by a leading nonviolent Palestinian organiser
Calls for concrete international action, not statements

stories.h: Gaza refugees in Egypt preyed on by fake charities
sum: Palestinians who fled Gaza to Egypt, barred from working and receiving little aid, are being targeted by fake charities and brokers, Mondoweiss reports with Egab. Phishing links shared in WhatsApp and Facebook groups collect passport photos and family details, then callers trick victims into handing over mobile-wallet codes; one refugee lost about $1,200.

Brokers also sell places on Gaza medical-evacuation lists and vanish, one man says, after taking $5,000. A lawyer says refugees without valid residency often cannot file police reports. Aid groups describe support drying up since the October 2025 ceasefire, and UNRWA does not operate in Egypt.
pts: One family paid over $100,000 to leave Gaza, then lost residency
Mondoweiss found no registration for a charity used in one scam
Overstay fines leave some refugees unable to travel
